title: Dimension complexity of distribution-independent SQ learning
formal: Is there a universal constant \(C>0\) with the following property? For every nonempty set \(X\), every nonempty binary concept class \(\mathcal H\subseteq\{-1,+1\}^{X}\), every integer \(m\ge1\), tolerance \(0<\tau<1\) and error \(0\le\varepsilon<1/4\), suppose a single randomized statistical-query learner makes at most \(m\) queries of tolerance \(\tau\) and, for every input distribution \(D\), target \(h\in\mathcal H\) and admissible oracle response rule, returns \(\hat h\) with \(\mathbb E[\Pr_{x\sim D}(\hat h(x)\ne h(x))]\le\varepsilon\). Must \(\operatorname{dc}(\mathcal H)\le C m/\tau^{2}\)? The learner is selected before the distribution, target and oracle replies. The constant is independent of all these objects and of the accuracy, domain size and class.
why: This asks whether learning successfully from noisy expectation information under every distribution forces all targets to share a small linear representation. It connects a general information-access model with the geometric capacity of linear predictors, and tests whether known advantages of learned representations depend essentially on the input distribution.
status_note: Open Question 2 in the COLT 2026 source. Bounded primary-source search on 2026-09-14 found the August 2026 VALG theorem, whose explicit additional rank hypothesis and polynomial bound do not settle the stated implication. The source also reports a flaw in the earlier 2025 claimed bound. This review compares theorem scope; it does not independently verify either paper’s proofs.

progress.text: Feldman, Kamath and Srebro state the linear dimension bound as Open Question 2. Their Section 3 reports that the claimed upper bounds of Karchmer and Malach (2025) have a proof flaw, citing a 2026 communication with those authors.

The VALG preprint presents Theorem 4.9 under the additional polynomial mean-response-rank hypothesis of Assumption 4.42. Its explicit qualification prevents treating it as a resolution of the unrestricted question. The theorem has not been independently proof-checked in this review.

sentences: The question asks whether successful distribution-independent statistical-query learning forces low dimension complexity.
The learner may adapt bounded expectation queries to previous noisy answers.
Its guarantee must hold for every distribution, target and valid response rule.
The desired conclusion is one deterministic feature map representing the entire class exactly in dimension proportional to the query count divided by squared tolerance.
Recent conditional results impose additional structure and do not establish the unrestricted implication.

definitions:
Use the discrete measurable structure \(2^{X}\) on an arbitrary domain, and quantify over all countably additive probability measures on it. A tolerance-\(\tau\) query is an arbitrary bounded function \(q:X\times\{-1,+1\}\to[-1,1]\); its answer is any real \(v\) satisfying \(|v-\mathbb E_{x\sim D}q(x,h(x))|\le\tau\). Queries may depend on previous answers and an internal random seed independent of the instance. A response rule can depend on the public history, including the current query, but observes the hidden seed only through that history. It must obey the tolerance at every history that can occur for the fixed distribution and target. The guarantee holds for every such rule, with expectation over the learner's seed. Require the interactions and their resulting loss to be measurable, so that the stated expectations exist. These measurable-interaction conventions specify the source's abstract oracle model. Query count is the resource: there is no restriction on computation between queries, description length, adaptivity, or the class containing the output predictor. There are no free samples or additional distribution information.

The dimension complexity is the least integer \(d\ge0\) for which there is one map \(\phi:X\to\mathbb R^{d}\) such that, for each \(h\in\mathcal H\), some \(w_h\in\mathbb R^{d}\) satisfies \(h(x)=\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(\langle w_h,\phi(x)\rangle)\) for every \(x\in X\). Here \(\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(z)=+1\) when \(z\ge0\), and \(-1\) otherwise, and the inner product is the sum of coordinatewise products. Put \(\operatorname{dc}=+\infty\) if no finite dimension works. The feature map is deterministic, shared by all targets, and independent of \(D\); no construction or efficiency requirement is imposed on it. Offsets require a coordinate of the feature map. The representation must be exact at every point, even though the learner's premise allows positive expected error.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof of the universal implication, or of its negation. A positive answer must supply a universal finite \(C\). A negative answer must show that no such constant works: for every \(C>0\), exhibit or prove the existence of a class and admissible learner parameters satisfying the premise but with \(\operatorname{dc}(\mathcal H)>Cm/\tau^{2}\). An infinite dimension example also qualifies. A result assuming extra rank, margin or distribution conditions, or allowing only approximate or random feature representations, does not establish the stated implication.

context_blocks.text: The source poses separate questions about a specified neural-network training procedure and about statistical queries. This card selects its formal Open Question 2. The broader deep-learning motivation is retained here; the card does not assert that this SQ question is equivalent to the neural-network question.

Learning may choose different predictors after observing different distributions. A low-dimensional representation has a stronger order of choices: the same features must work before either the distribution or the target is selected. Exact representation also concerns points that may have negligible probability in a particular learning instance.

The statistical-query interface permits queries that depend jointly on the example and its label. Restricting queries to a label multiplied by an example function gives a different model. Similarly, replacing the requested bound by an unspecified polynomial, or adding dependence on the domain size, changes the question.

The August 2026 preprint gives a conditional polynomial dimension statement. It assumes a bound on the dimension of a space of averaged terminal predictions; that bound is an additional hypothesis, not a consequence established for arbitrary SQ learners. Its authors explicitly describe the remaining gap to the original question.
